findings.title: Recognition Overflows Into Witness
findings.claim: In 5:83, receiving what was sent down moves through hearing and recognition into visible overflow of the eyes, then into spoken faith and a request to be counted among witnesses.
findings.mechanism: The focus places hearing before recognition from the truth, makes the eyes the subject of overflow from tears, and follows that bodily response with saying, faith, inscription, accompaniment, and witnesses; the sequence turns inward reception into public petition.
findings.reader_payoff: The tears become a visible threshold between knowing and saying, while the final request appears as the social continuation of recognition rather than an isolated closing phrase.
findings.containment: This adds a reception-to-public-petition movement to the ordinary scene. It treats tears as the visible response supplied by the focus and does not claim that bodily response proves sincerity or establishes a wider doctrine of witnesshood.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and occurrences are supplied exactly and the channel nomination is trusted, while the combined sequence remains an interpretive relation rather than a grammatical paraphrase.
